title: Projection Predictive Inference for Generalized Linear and Additive Multilevel Models
file_name: Projection Predictive Inference for Generalized Linear and Additive Multilevel Models.md
universal_lens: Projection predictive inference establishes a rigorous isomorphism between high-dimensional posterior estimation and low-dimensional decision-making. By decoupling the reference model from variable selection, it projects the full posterior onto constrained subspaces using Kullback-Leibler divergence minimization, preserving predictive fidelity while drastically reducing structural complexity.
gsi_mapping: In Galaxy Sports Intelligence, this primitive maps to hierarchical Bayesian player valuation. A saturated GLMM capturing all biomechanical and contextual features serves as the reference. Projection sequentially isolates core performance drivers, yielding parsimonious conformal prediction sets that quantify uncertainty for real-time athlete projections.
gse_mapping: For Galaxy Sports Engine, projection predictive inference drives dynamic state-transition modeling. As game states evolve, the engine projects complex multilevel interactions onto minimal feature subsets relevant to the current tactical context, ensuring computationally efficient, robust situational reasoning without sacrificing predictive accuracy.

primitives.name: Posterior Projection Operator
primitives.verbatim_quote: Given a reference model on the basis of all variables, it aims at replacing its posterior _p_ ( _λ_ ∗ | D) with a constrained projection _q_ ⊥( _λ_ ).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: p(λ*|D): Full posterior probability density over complete parameter space λ* (dimensionless). q⊥(λ): Constrained projected posterior density over reduced parameter subset λ (dimensionless). D: Observed dataset.
primitives.assumptions: The reference model accurately captures the underlying data-generating process; the constrained subspace is nested within the full parameter space.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Fails if the reference model is severely misspecified or if the reduced subspace lacks sufficient expressive power to approximate the predictive distribution of the full model.

layer2.mapping: Mathematically equivalent to finding the closest distribution in a restricted manifold under KL divergence, directly mapping to GSI's need for parsimonious yet highly accurate predictive distributions.
layer2.telemetry: Kullback-Leibler divergence between the reference predictive distribution and the projected predictive distribution.

primitives.name: Sequential Variable Selection
primitives.verbatim_quote: Variable selection is then performed by sequentially adding relevant variables until predictive performance is satisfactory.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: Relevant variables: Covariates contributing significantly to predictive log-density (dimensionless). Predictive performance: Measured via out-of-sample expected log predictive density (ELPD) or cross-validation scores (nats).
primitives.assumptions: Marginal contributions of variables can be evaluated independently given previously selected variables; diminishing returns apply to added complexity.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down in the presence of severe multicollinearity where multiple correlated variables provide identical marginal gains, leading to arbitrary selection paths.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSE's greedy algorithmic approach for identifying critical tactical shifts, sequentially adding state variables only when they demonstrably improve the predictive horizon of the game engine.
layer2.telemetry: Incremental change in leave-one-out cross-validation (LOO-CV) score per added covariate.

primitives.name: Multilevel Structure Extension
primitives.verbatim_quote: In this work, we extend projection predictive inference to support variable and structure selection for generalized linear multilevel models (GLMMs) and generalized additive multilevel models (GAMMs).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: GLMMs: Generalized Linear Mixed Models incorporating random effects for grouped data (dimensionless parameters). GAMMs: Generalized Additive Mixed Models incorporating smooth non-linear functions (dimensionless).
primitives.assumptions: Random effects follow specified Gaussian priors; smooth terms can be approximated via penalized splines; Laplace approximation holds for marginal likelihood integration.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Laplace approximation fails in highly non-Gaussian random effect distributions or extreme boundary cases where the Hessian matrix becomes singular.

layer2.mapping: Directly unifies with GSI's hierarchical athlete-team dynamics, allowing simultaneous selection of fixed global features and local team-specific random effects without overfitting.
layer2.telemetry: Ratio of variance explained by selected random effects versus total residual variance.

reasoning_traces.think:
The core mathematical derivation hinges on the separation of estimation and decision. We begin with a saturated reference model, typically a complex GLMM or GAMM, which yields a high-dimensional posterior distribution p(λ*|D). The objective is not to estimate these parameters directly for inference, but to utilize them to construct a lower-dimensional projection q⊥(λ). This projection is defined as the distribution within a constrained subspace that minimizes the Kullback-Leibler divergence to the reference predictive distribution. By doing so, we effectively transfer the predictive information from the complex model to a simpler one. The sequential variable selection acts as a greedy optimization over the subspace lattice, evaluating the marginal gain in predictive log-density for each candidate variable. The extension to multilevel structures introduces a Laplace approximation to handle the intractable integrals over random effects, ensuring computational feasibility. The dualities lie in balancing model complexity against predictive accuracy, while failure modes emerge when the reference model is fundamentally flawed or when collinearity obscures the marginal contributions of variables, causing the projection to collapse into an overly sparse or biased representation.

reasoning_traces.retrocausal_genealogy: This framework inherits from classical Bayesian decision theory, specifically the works of Berger on formal hypothesis testing and decision rules. It evolves the traditional stepwise regression methods by embedding them within a rigorous probabilistic projection manifold. Historically, it bridges the gap between frequentist penalized likelihood approaches like LASSO and fully Bayesian hierarchical modeling, offering a unified perspective that respects both predictive utility and structural interpretability in complex statistical environments.
reasoning_traces.theory_of_mind: From a decision-theoretic standpoint, the 'agent' is the statistical model itself, acting on behalf of a user who desires parsimony without sacrificing accuracy. The opposing force is the inherent noise and complexity of the real-world data-generating process. The projection operator models the agent's belief that a simpler world exists beneath the observed chaos. It anticipates that the user will penalize unnecessary complexity, thus strategically selecting only those variables that provide a decisive edge in predictive performance, effectively playing a game of efficiency against the entropy of the data.
reasoning_traces.cross_layer_veto: A critical veto condition arises when the correlation structure among covariates induces severe multicollinearity. In such regimes, the marginal predictive gains of individual variables become indistinguishable, leading the sequential selector to arbitrarily pick proxies rather than true causal drivers. Furthermore, if the reference model suffers from significant specification errors—such as omitted non-linearities that cannot be captured by the GAMM smooth terms—the projection will faithfully replicate these biases. Therefore, a cross-layer validation must veto any projection that exhibits high variance in variable selection across bootstrap resamples, indicating instability in the underlying epistemic foundation.
